segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Hello, Helen. Sorry I’m late.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Hi, Jeremy, no problem. Well we’d better work out where we are on our project, I suppose.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Yeah. I’ve looked at the drawings you’ve done for my story, ‘The Forest’, and I think they’re brilliant – they really create the atmosphere I had in mind when I was writing it.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I’m glad you like them.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: There are just a few suggestions I’d like to make.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Go ahead.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Now, I’m not sure about the drawing of the cave – it’s got trees all around it, which is great, but the drawing’s a bit too static, isn’t it? I think it needs some action.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Yes, there’s nothing happening. Perhaps I should add the boy – Malcolm, isn’t it? He would be walking up to it.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Yes, let’s have Malcolm in the drawing. And what about putting in a tiger – the one that he makes friends with a bit later? Maybe it could be sitting under a tree washing itself.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: And the tiger stops in the middle of what it’s doing when it sees Malcolm walking past.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: That’s a good idea.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: OK, I’ll have a go at that.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Then there’s the drawing of the crowd of men and women dancing. They’re just outside the forest, and there’s a lot going on.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: That’s right, you wanted them to be watching a carnival procession, but I thought it would be too crowded. Do you think it works like this?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Yes, I like what you’ve done. The only thing is, could you add Malcolm to it, without changing what’s already there.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: What about having him sitting on the tree trunk on the right of the picture?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Yes, that would be fine.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: And do you want him watching the other people?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: No, he’s been left out of all the fun, so I’d like him to be crying – that’ll contrast nicely with the next picture, where he’s laughing at the clowns in the carnival.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Right, I’ll do that.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: And then the drawing of the people ice skating in the forest.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: I wasn’t too happy with that one. Because they’re supposed to be skating on grass aren’t they?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: That’s right, and it’s frozen over. At the moment it doesn’t look quite right.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Mm, I see what you mean. I’ll have another go at that.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: And I like the wool hats they’re wearing. Maybe you could give each of them a scarf as well.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Yeah, that’s easy enough. They can be streaming out behind the people to suggest they’re skating really fast.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Mm, great. Well that’s all on the drawings.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Right. So you’ve finished writing your story and I just need to finish illustrating it, and my story and your drawings are done. ———————–

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: So the next thing is to decide what exactly we need to write about in the report that goes with the stories, and how we’re going to divide the work.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Right, Helen.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: What do you think about including a section on how we planned the project as a whole, Jeremy? That’s probably quite important.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Yeah. Well, you’ve had most of the good ideas so far. How do you feel about drafting something, then we can go through it together and discuss it?

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: OK, that seems reasonable. And I could include something on how we came up with the ideas for our two stories, couldn’t I?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: Well, I’ve started writing something about that, so why don’t you do the same and we can include the two things.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Right. So what about our interpretation of the stories? Do we need to write about what we think they show, like the value of helping other people, all that sort of thing?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: That’s going to come up later isn’t it? I think everyone in the class is going to read each other’s stories and come up with their own interpretations which we’re going to discuss.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Oh, I missed that. So it isn’t going to be part of the report at all?

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: No. But we need to write about the illustrations, because they’re an essential element of children’s experience of reading the stories. It’s probably easiest for you to write that section, as you know more about drawing than I do.

segments.speaker: HELEN
segments.en: Maybe, but I find it quite hard to write about. I’d be happier if you did it.

segments.speaker: JEREMY
segments.en: OK. So when do you think ...

SECTION 3
Questions 21-30
ILLUSTRATION PROJECT
Complete the table below. Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer.
Table Rows:
      A [21] __________ surrounded by trees
      Add Malcolm and a [22] __________ noticing him
      People who are [23] __________ outside the forest
      Add Malcolm sitting on a tree trunk and [24] __________
      Ice-skaters on [25] __________ covered with ice
      Add a [26] __________ for each person
Table Headers:
    Subject of drawing
    Change to be made
Report Parts
Who is going to write each of the following parts of the report?
Write the correct letter A–D next to questions 27–30.
Items:
    Q Num: 27
    Text: how they planned the project
    Q Num: 28
    Text: how they had ideas for their stories
    Q Num: 29
    Text: an interpretation of their stories
    Q Num: 30
    Text: comments on the illustrations
Options:
    Id: A
    Text: Helen only
    Id: B
    Text: Jeremy only
    Id: C
    Text: both Helen and Jeremy
    Id: D
    Text: neither Helen nor Jeremy
